page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the c3d server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The c3d-highcpu-4 demonstrates strong single-core performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU benchmarks, and achieves average scores in single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations are significantly constrained. Multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core scores, and software compilation benchmarks fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with Passmark memory scores in the bottom 10% and uncached memory write bandwidth limited to 15.4 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the c3d-highcpu-4 is its low memory density and weak multi-threaded scaling, which limits its utility for memory-intensive databases or parallelized compilation tasks. It is qualitatively a cost-efficient entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require large memory footprints or local storage. This instance is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, basic text processing, or small-scale model inference, such as text generation with small 135M parameter language models where it maintains average performance.

It features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of RAM, and no local storage or GPU resources.
